Progress

Guardrail: a safety layer for language-commanded drones

A safety layer between a drone's AI pilot (VLA) and its autopilot (ArduPilot): flight rules are written once in a file, summarised for the AI, and checked on every command before it reaches the drone.

The problem

A VLA (Vision-Language-Action model: it reads camera images and a text instruction and outputs motion commands) can output a command that breaks a flight rule, for example flying into a no-fly zone (NFZ). The grant asks for a system in which no P0 (highest-priority) rule violation reaches the aircraft, and for numbers that prove it.

The approach

The work packages: WP1 writes the rules in a Policy DSL (a fixed YAML/JSON rule format) and packs them into a signed bundle (an archive of the rules with a hash and a signature). WP2, the Prefix Compiler, turns the rules into a CSP (Constraint Summary Pack) for the VLA's prompt. WP3, the Safety Shield, checks and repairs every command; in the grant's design, ArduPilot's own GeoFence (the autopilot's built-in boundary) and its RTL (return to launch) / Land modes sit behind it as the last backstop. WP4 delivers the stress scenarios that produce the KPI numbers.

Five roles in one picture

1

The driver: decides where to go, and may make mistakes.

The pilot: a VLA (OpenVLA-7B and AerialVLA have flown through the Shield in simulation). The city demonstrations use a hand-written test controller in its place.

2

The rulebook: 'do not drive here', 'max 5 m/s'.

The policy: a YAML file in policies/, parsed by guardrail/models.py and hashed.

3

The driving instructor with a second brake pedal: corrects or stops the driver.

The Safety Shield: checks every command against all rules before it is sent.

4

The car and its engine: does what it is told.

ArduPilot (the autopilot) plus a simulator.

5

The black box: records every decision on which a command would have broken a rule.

The audit log (audit.jsonl), written by guardrail/audit.py.

Work packages

WP1

Policy DSL / IR / signed bundle

A fixed way to write flight rules in a YAML or JSON file (Policy DSL), and the parsed in-memory form that other parts read (IR). The rules are packed into a signed bundle with a hash, so a flight can later be checked against the exact rules it used.

5 built 2 next

WP2

Prefix Constraint Compiler

Turns the policy into a short Constraint Summary Pack (CSP) for the VLA's prompt, so that the VLA knows the rules before it chooses an action. The goal is fewer rule-breaking commands, so the Shield has less to repair.

5 built 2 next

WP3

Suffix Safety Shield

WP3 delivers a ROS 2 node between the VLA and MAVROS 2 that checks every command and repairs it if it would break a rule. In the grant's design it also escalates to Brake, Loiter, RTL or Land when a repair is not safe, with ArduPilot's own GeoFence as the last backstop.

6 built 3 next

WP4

Dynamic-scenario stress testing

WP4 delivers a library of test scenarios in which rules change mid-flight (moving NFZ, time-window switch, corridor swap), and a harness that runs them and computes the KPIs. Under the grant, every KPI in the final report comes from this harness.

5 built 6 next
